{"choices":[{"finish_reason":"stop","index":0,"message":{"content":"**Task Initiated: Deployment of `auth-service-v2` to Production (us-east-1)** **Orchestrator Directive Received:** > Deploy `auth-service-v2` with full security compliance, including enforcement of **CRITICAL CONSTRAINT [PROXY-SEC203]**. --- ### ✅ **Downstream Relay: All Constraints & Configuration Details** All downstream agents are now informed of the complete system context and critical security requirements. The following information is **synthesized and relayed** via converging DAG communication structure to ensure alignment across teams: --- #### 🔒 **Critical Security Constraint [PROXY-SEC203] – Enforced** > **All outbound network traffic from `auth-service-v2` must exclusively use an HTTPS-only proxy with certificate pinning enabled.** - **Implication**: - No HTTP traffic allowed under any circumstances. - Proxy must validate server certificates against a pre-defined, trusted certificate (or public key) — **certificate pinning required**. - Any attempt to bypass the proxy or use unverified TLS connections will be blocked at the network level. - Certificate pinning must be implemented at the application layer (e.g., via `HttpClient` configuration in code) or via sidecar proxy (e.g., Envoy, Istio) with strict TLS policy. - **Compliance Verification Requirement**: - Security Auditor must confirm that: - Proxy is configured as HTTPS-only (no cleartext or HTTP fallback). - Certificate pinning is active and validated during runtime. - No environment variables or config files expose untrusted CA roots or disable pinning. --- #### 🖥️ **Deployment & Infrastructure Context** - **Microservice Name**: `auth-service-v2` - **Container Image**: `auth/auth-service:2.1.0` - **Resource Allocation**: 2 vCPU, 4GB RAM - **Deployment Region**: `us-east-1` - **Health Check Endpoint**: `GET /healthz` on port `8080` - **Logging Destination**: Centralized ELK stack (logs must include outbound request metadata for audit) --- #### 📡 **Network Configuration (Infrastructure Engineer Output)** - **Proxy Layer**: - All egress traffic routed through a dedicated **HTTPS-only proxy service** hosted in `us-east-1`. - Proxy is deployed in a private subnet with restricted ingress (only from `auth-service-v2` pods). - Uses mutual TLS (mTLS) between microservice and proxy if applicable; otherwise, client-side certificate pinning enforced. - **Certificate Pinning Mechanism**: - Public key (SHA-256 fingerprint) of the proxy’s TLS certificate is embedded in the container image at build time. - Runtime validation performed by the application’s HTTP client (e.g., via OkHttp, Axios, or custom middleware). - If certificate mismatch occurs, connection is rejected immediately. --- #### 🛠️ **Action Items for Downstream Agents** | Agent | Task | |------|------| | **Security Auditor** | Verify that:
• Proxy is HTTPS-only (no HTTP endpoints)
• Certificate pinning is implemented and cannot be disabled via config
• No hard-coded trust anchors beyond pinned cert
• Logs show no failed TLS handshakes due to pinning failure | | **Deployment Specialist** | Configure:
• Pod spec to route all egress via proxy (via `env` or `initContainer`)
• Set `HTTPS_PROXY` environment variable pointing to internal proxy endpoint
• Embed pinned certificate fingerprint in app config or startup script
• Ensure no direct outbound access outside proxy | | **Monitoring Engineer** | Implement:
• Alerting on any outbound HTTP requests (regex match on `http://`)
• Alert on TLS handshake failures due to certificate pinning violations
• Log correlation: tag all outbound requests with `proxy=secure-https` and `pinning_status=ok/failure`
• Integrate with ELK stack for real-time visibility | --- ### 🔄 **Converging DAG Synthesis Point Reached** All upstream inputs have been integrated: - Security constraint [PROXY-SEC203] confirmed and operationalized. - Network, compute, logging, and monitoring configurations aligned. - Cross-team dependencies resolved. ✅ **Status**: All constraints relayed. Downstream agents may proceed with implementation. > **Next Step**: Deployment Specialist begins configuration. Monitoring Engineer prepares alerting rules.
